vsm1.8:130.1: There are two kinds of blood: stored blood and mobile blood.
vsm1.8:130.2:
Herein, as to colour, stored blood is the colour of cooked and thickened lac solution;
mobile blood is the colour of clear lac solution.
vsm1.8:130.3: As to shape, both are the shape of their locations.
vsm1.8:130.4: As to direction, the stored blood belongs to the upper direction; the other belongs to both directions.
vsm1.8:130.5:
As to location, except for the fleshless parts of the head hairs, body hairs, teeth, nails, and the hard dry skin,
the mobile blood permeates the whole of the clung-to (kammically-acquired) body by following the network of veins.
vsm1.8:130.6:
The stored blood fills the lower part of the liver’s site to the extent of a bowlful, and by its splashing
little by little over the heart, kidney and lungs, it keeps the kidney, heart, liver and lungs moist. For it
is when it fails to moisten the kidney, heart, etc., that beings become thirsty.
vsm1.8:130.7: As to delimitation, it is bounded by what appertains to blood
vsm1.8:130.8: This is its delimitation by the similar. But its delimitation by the dissimilar is like that for the head hairs.
vsm1.8:131.1: This is the water element that trickles from the pores of the body hairs, and so on.
vsm1.8:131.2: As to colour, it is the colour of clear sesame oil.
vsm1.8:131.3: As to shape, it is the shape of its location.
vsm1.8:131.4: As to direction, it belongs to both directions.
vsm1.8:131.5: As to location, there is no fixed location for sweat where it could always be found like blood.
vsm1.8:131.6:
But if the body is heated by the heat of a fire, by the sun’s heat, by a change of temperature, etc., then it trickles from all the
pore openings of the head hairs and body hairs, as water does from a bunch of unevenly cut lily-bud stems and lotus stalks pulled
up from the water. So its shape should also be understood to correspond to the pore-openings of the head hairs and body hairs.
vsm1.8:131.7:
And the meditator who discerns sweat should only give his attention to it as it is to be found
filling the pore-openings of the head hairs and body hairs.
vsm1.8:131.8: As to delimitation, it is bounded by what appertains to sweat
vsm1.8:131.9: This is its delimitation by the similar. But its delimitation by the dissimilar is like that for the head hairs.
vsm1.8:132.2: As to colour, it is the colour of sliced turmeric.
vsm1.8:132.3:
As to shape, firstly in the body of a stout man it is the shape of turmeric-coloured
dukūla (muslin) rags placed between the inner skin and the flesh.
vsm1.8:132.4:
In the body of a lean man it is the shape of turmeric-coloured dukūla (muslin) rags placed in two or three
thicknesses on the shank flesh, thigh flesh, back flesh near the spine, and belly-covering flesh.
vsm1.8:132.5: As to direction, it belongs to both directions.
vsm1.8:132.6:
As to location, it permeates the whole of a stout man’s body; it is to be found on a lean man’s
shank flesh, and so on. And though it was described as “unguent” above, still it is neither used
as oil on the head nor as oil for the nose, etc., because of its utter disgustingness.
vsm1.8:132.7: As to delimitation, it is bounded below by the flesh, above by the inner skin, and all round by what appertains to fat
vsm1.8:132.8: This is its delimitation by the similar. But its delimitation by the dissimilar is like that for the head hairs.
vsm1.8:133.1: These are the water element that trickles from the eye.
vsm1.8:133.2: As to colour, they are the colour of clear sesame oil.
vsm1.8:133.3: As to shape, they are the shape of their location.
vsm1.8:133.4: As to direction, they belong to the upper direction.
vsm1.8:133.5: As to location, they are to be found in the eye sockets.
vsm1.8:133.6: But they are not stored in the eye sockets all the while as the bile is in the bile container.
vsm1.8:133.7:
But when beings feel joy and laugh uproariously, or feel grief and weep and lament, or eat particular
kinds of wrong food, or when their eyes are affected by smoke, dust, dirt, etc., then being originated by the joy,
grief, wrong food, or temperature, they fill up the eye sockets or trickle out.
vsm1.8:133.8: And the meditator who discerns tears should discern them only as they are to be found filling the eye sockets.
vsm1.8:133.9: As to delimitation, they are bounded by what appertains to tears
vsm1.8:133.10: This is its delimitation by the similar. But its delimitation by the dissimilar is like that for the head hairs.
vsm1.8:134.2: As to colour, it is the colour of coconut oil. Also it can be said to be the colour of oil sprinkled on gruel.
vsm1.8:134.3: As to shape, it is a film the shape of a drop of unguent spread out over still water at the time of bathing.
vsm1.8:134.4: As to direction, it belongs to both directions.
vsm1.8:134.5:
As to location, it is to be found mostly on the palms of the hands, backs of the hands, soles of the feet,
backs of the feet, tip of the nose, forehead, and points of the shoulders.
vsm1.8:134.6:
And it is not always to be found in the melted state in these locations, but when these parts get hot with the heat of a fire,
the sun’s heat, upset of temperature or upset of elements, then it spreads here and there in those places
like the film from the drop of unguent on the still water at the time of bathing.
vsm1.8:134.7: As to delimitation, it is bounded by what appertains to grease
vsm1.8:134.8: This is its delimitation by the similar. But its delimitation by the dissimilar is like that for the head hairs.
vsm1.8:135.1: This is water element mixed with froth inside the mouth.
vsm1.8:135.2: As to colour, it is white, the colour of the froth.
vsm1.8:135.3: As to shape, it is the shape of its location, or it can be called “the shape of froth.”
vsm1.8:135.4: As to direction, it belongs to the upper direction.
vsm1.8:135.5: As to location, it is to be found on the tongue after it has descended from the cheeks on both sides.
vsm1.8:135.6: And it is not always to be found stored there;
vsm1.8:135.7:
but when beings see particular kinds of food, or remember them, or put something hot or bitter or sharp
or salty or sour into their mouths, or when their hearts are faint, or nausea arises on some account,
then spittle appears and runs down from the cheeks on both sides to settle on the tongue.
vsm1.8:135.8:
It is thin at the tip of the tongue, and thick at the root of the tongue. It is capable,
without getting used up, of wetting unhusked rice or husked rice or anything else chewable
that is put into the mouth, like the water in a pit scooped out in a river sand bank.
vsm1.8:135.9: As to delimitation, it is bounded by what appertains to spittle
vsm1.8:135.10: This is its delimitation by the similar. But its delimitation by the dissimilar is like that for the head hairs.
vsm1.8:136.1: This is impurity that trickles out from the brain.
vsm1.8:136.2: As to colour, it is the colour of a young palmyra kernel.
vsm1.8:136.3: As to shape, it is the shape of its location.
vsm1.8:136.4: As to direction, it belongs to the upper direction.
vsm1.8:136.5: As to location, it is to be found filling the nostril cavities.
vsm1.8:136.6:
And it is not always to be found stored there; but rather, just as though a man tied up curd in a lotus leaf,
which he then pricked with a thorn underneath, and whey oozed out and dripped,
vsm1.8:136.7:
so too, when beings weep or suffer a disturbance of elements produced by wrong food or temperature,
then the brain inside the head turns into stale phlegm, and it oozes out and comes
down by an opening in the palate, and it fills the nostrils and stays there or trickles out.
vsm1.8:136.8: And the meditator who discerns snot should discern it only as it is to be found filling the nostril cavities.
vsm1.8:136.9: As to delimitation, it is bounded by what appertains to snot
vsm1.8:136.10: This is its delimitation by the similar. But its delimitation by the dissimilar is like that for the head hairs.
vsm1.8:137.1: This is the slimy ordure inside the joints in the body.
vsm1.8:137.2: As to colour, it is the colour of kaṇikāra gum.
vsm1.8:137.3: As to shape, it is the shape of its location.
vsm1.8:137.4: As to direction, it belongs to both directions.
vsm1.8:137.5: As to location, it is to be found inside the hundred and eighty joints, serving the function of lubricating the bones’ joints.
vsm1.8:137.6:
If it is weak, when a man gets up or sits down, moves forward or backward, bends or stretches,
then his bones creak, and he goes about making a noise like the snapping of fingers, and when he has walked
only one or two leagues’ distance, his air element gets upset and his limbs pain him.
vsm1.8:137.7:
But if a man has plenty of it, his bones do not creak when he gets up, sits down, etc., and even when he
has walked a long distance, his air element does not get upset and his limbs do not pain him.
vsm1.8:137.8: As to delimitation, it is bounded by what appertains to oil of the joints
vsm1.8:137.9: This is its delimitation by the similar. But its delimitation by the dissimilar is like that for the head hairs.
vsm1.8:138.2: As to colour, it is the colour of bean brine.
vsm1.8:138.3: As to shape, it is the shape of water inside a water pot placed upside down.
vsm1.8:138.4: As to direction, it belongs to the lower direction.
vsm1.8:138.5: As to location, it is to be found inside the bladder. For the bladder sack is called the bladder.
vsm1.8:138.6:
Just as when a porous pot with no mouth is put into a cesspool, then the solution from the cesspool gets into the porous
pot with no mouth even though no way of entry is evident, so too, while the urinary secretion from the body
enters the bladder its way of entry is not evident. Its way of exit, however, is evident.
vsm1.8:138.7: And when the bladder is full of urine, beings feel the need to make water.
vsm1.8:138.8: As to delimitation, it is delimited by the inside of the bladder and by what is similar to urine.
vsm1.8:138.9: This is the delimitation by the similar.
vsm1.8:138.10: But its delimitation by the dissimilar is like that for the head hairs (see note at end of §90).
vsm1.8:139.1:
When the meditator has defined the parts beginning with the head hairs in this way by colour, shape,
direction, location and delimitation (§58), and he gives his attention in the ways beginning with “following
the order, not too quickly” (§61) to their repulsiveness in the five aspects of colour, shape,
smell, habitat, and location (§84f.), then at last he surmounts the concept (§66).
vsm1.8:139.2:
Then just as when a man with good sight is observing a garland of flowers of thirty-two colours knotted on a single
string and all the flowers become evident to him simultaneously, so too, when the meditator observes this body thus,
“There are in this body head hairs,” then all these things become evident to him, as it were, simultaneously.
vsm1.8:139.3:
Hence it was said above in the explanation of skill in giving attention: “For when a beginner gives his attention to head hairs,
his attention carries on till it arrives at the last part, that is, urine, and stops there” (§67).
vsm1.8:140.1:
If he applies his attention externally as well when all the parts have become evident in this way, then human beings, animals,
etc., as they go about are divested of their aspect of beings and appear as just assemblages of parts. And when drink,
food, etc., is being swallowed by them, it appears as though it were being put in among the assemblage of parts.
vsm1.8:141.1:
Then, as he gives his attention to them again and again as “Repulsive, repulsive,” employing
the process of “successive leaving,” etc. (§67), eventually absorption arises in him.
vsm1.8:141.2:
Herein, the appearance of the head hairs, etc., as to colour, shape, direction, location, and delimitation
is the learning sign; their appearance as repulsive in all aspects is the counterpart sign.
vsm1.8:141.3:
As he cultivates and develops that counterpart sign, absorption arises in him, but only of the first
jhāna, in the same way as described under foulness as a meditation subject (VI.64f.).
vsm1.8:141.4:
And it arises singly in one to whom only one part has become evident, or who has reached
absorption in one part and makes no further effort about another.
vsm1.8:142.1:
But several first jhānas, according to the number of parts, are produced in one to whom several parts have become
evident, or who has reached jhāna in one and also makes further effort about another. As in the case of the Elder Mallaka.
vsm1.8:142.2:
The elder, it seems, took the Elder Abhaya, the Dīgha reciter, by the hand, and after
saying “Friend Abhaya, first learn this matter,” he went on:
vsm1.8:142.3:
“The Elder Mallaka is an obtainer of thirty-two jhānas in the thirty-two parts.
If he enters upon one by night and one by day, he goes on entering upon them for over a fortnight; but if
he enters upon one each day, he goes on entering upon them for over a month.”
vsm1.8:143.1:
And although this meditation is successful in this way with the first jhāna, it is nevertheless called “mindfulness
occupied with the body” because it is successful through the influence of the mindfulness of the colour, shape, and so on.
vsm1.8:144.1:
And the bhikkhu who is devoted to this mindfulness occupied with the body “is a conqueror of boredom and delight,
and boredom does not conquer him; he dwells transcending boredom as it arises.
vsm1.8:144.2: He is a conqueror of fear and dread, and fear and dread do not conquer him; he dwells transcending fear and dread as they arise.
vsm1.8:144.3: He is one who bears cold and heat … who endures … arisen bodily feelings that are … menacing to life” (M III 97);
vsm1.8:144.4: he becomes an obtainer of the four jhānas based on the colour aspect of the head hairs, etc.;
vsm1.8:144.5: and he comes to penetrate the six kinds of direct-knowledge (see MN 6).
vsm1.8:144.6:
So let a man, if he is wise,
Untiringly devote his days
To mindfulness of body which
Rewards him in so many ways.
vsm1.8:144.7: This is the section dealing with mindfulness occupied with the body in the detailed treatise.
